text:
sam: FYI rolled driver 535.86 -> 535.90 + kernel 6.2.15 to us-east1-gpu-pool ~12:10 UTC. Seeing ~30 nodes where MIG partitions appear/disappear intermittently. Pods requesting 2g/1g scheduled then fail with device attach errors or OOMs.

infra-bot: deploy finished to us-east1-gpu-pool at 2026-03-17T12:10:12Z :rocket:

alex: Confirmed. Quick sample from one affected node (nvidia-smi -L then mig list):
```
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: A100-SXM4 (UUID: GPU-AAAA1111)
  MIG 1g.5gb Device 0 (UUID: MIG-OLD-1111)
  MIG 2g.10gb Device 1 (UUID: MIG-OLD-2222)

$ nvidia-smi mig -i 0 -L
GPU 0: A100-SXM4 (UUID: GPU-AAAA1111)
  MIG devices: none

# after a few seconds
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: A100-SXM4 (UUID: GPU-AAAA1111)
  MIG 1g.5gb Device 0 (UUID: MIG-NEW-9999)
```
Looks like UUIDs flip and sometimes the MIG devices vanish. Scheduler tries to attach old UUID and fails.

jenny: kubectl describe pod shows: "FailedStart: failed to attach device: requested MIG UUID MIG-OLD-1111 not found on node". I grabbed kubelet/device-plugin logs, lots of `device not found` + `device plugin: failed to allocate`.

priya: hypothesis: kernel+driver bump changed the order/timestamp of udev or the new nvidia-mig-manager recomputes partition UUIDs if metadata isn't persisted. Could be race in mig-manager startup vs kubelet device plugin. Check /var/lib/nvidia/mig/metadata and `/etc/nvidia/mig.conf` pinning flags.

alex: rolled back one node to 535.86 (manually) and its MIG config stayed stable. Rolling back seems to restore expected UUIDs on that host.

sam: Pause the global rollout. Priya, can you draft a short runbook for triage + rollback? Jenny/lex: collect the following from affected nodes:
- journalctl -u nvidia-mig-manager -o short-iso --since "12:00" > /tmp/mig-logs.txt
- sudo cat /var/lib/nvidia/mig/metadata/* > /tmp/mig-metadata.txt
- nvidia-smi -L and `nvidia-smi mig -i <gpu> -l` outputs
- kubelet & device-plugin logs (kubectl logs)

jenny: On it. uploading logs to GCS `/infra/mig-incident/1864123456/`. linking in a sec. Also saw some nodes with dkms warnings during kernel module reload.

release-bot: rollback triggered for us-east1-gpu-pool at 2026-03-17T12:37:20Z by @sam

priya: TL;DR action items: 1) stop rollout to other zones, 2) roll affected nodes back to 535.86 where possible, 3) collect mig-manager + udev logs to confirm startup ordering, 4) add temporary mig-manager delay until kubelet device-plugin is ready, 5) prepare a safe re-roll plan (pin MIG UUIDs or persist metadata).

alex: note — eu-west1 and ap-south unaffected so far. Blast radius limited to us-east1 pool (mixed spot/preemptible). If we rollback we lose ~10% utilization for a few hours while nodes re-drain; cost/availability trade-off.

sam: agreed. Priya please create an incident doc with timeline and link to logs. I'll coordinate on the rollback window and notify SRE on-call.

jenny: uploaded logs and a quick grep: `grep -E "error|warn|failed" /tmp/mig-logs.txt | head -n 50` shows repeated `udev: device disappeared` right after `mig-manager: applied partitions`. Putting more details in the incident doc. :mag_right:
